subject: Onboarding: W-9 proxy signer + escrow custodian — PO activation roadmap
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding: W-9 proxy signer + escrow custodian — PO activation roadmap

Hi Marta —

Quick follow-up from our onboarding call this morning. BlueHarbor indicated the W-9 will be signed by a proxy (local finance agent) rather than the corporate officer listed on the legal entity record. Before Procurement can clear the PO we need two things clarified:  

1) Signatory authority: please confirm the proxy signer name, title, and attach a short delegation letter (signed by an officer) or notarized authorization. We can accept DocuSign with an attached PDF of the delegation if that is easier.

2) Escrow custodian: your onboarding notes mentioned using an escrow custodian for the initial milestone (vendor requested for first 30 days). Provide the escrow company name and their standard agreement — Procurement needs to validate KYC and fee schedule. If escrow requires vendor-side KYC, let us know the expected timeline.

Attached is our W-9 template for reference (redwood-w9-template.pdf) — we prefer an IRS-acceptable TIN confirmation where possible. If you cannot provide a notarized W-9, a DocuSigned W-9 plus the delegation letter will usually suffice for PO activation.

Target: if we receive delegation + signed W-9 + escrow agreement by EOD Tuesday (2025-04-15), we can finalize PO-7842 and release the first milestone the following week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Manager, Procurement
Redwood Inference

Date: 2025-04-12T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: EscrowCo: Custodian steps & KYC requirements for BlueHarbor

Hi Jonas / Ben / Marta —

Samir here from EscrowCo. We can onboard BlueHarbor as the vendor-facing beneficiary for a time-limited milestone escrow. High-level KYC checklist we need from the beneficiary:  

- Registered business name and EIN (copy of W-9 is fine)
- Beneficial owner confirmation (UBO) — short form acceptable for corporate entities
- Photo ID for the delegated signer (Diego Morales) and a copy of the delegation letter
- Escrow agreement signature by an authorized officer (we can accept DocuSign)

Typical timeline: KYC + agreement execution: 2–4 business days once we have all documents. Fees are one-time: $350 for the escrow setup + $25/month custodial fee for the period the funds are held. We can provide a redlineable agreement — attaching our onboarding packet (escrow_custodian_instructions.pdf).

If Redwood prefers the vendor to provide an IRS 147C (TIN acceptance letter) we can accept that in lieu of additional verification, but our onboarding still requires ID for the delegated signer.

Happy to schedule a 20-min call to walk through the agreement if helpful.

Best,
Samir Patel
Head of Onboarding
EscrowCo

Jonas / Laura —

Acknowledged. BlueHarbor’s materials look mostly in order. Procurement finance will hold PO-7842 in 'staged' until we complete two verifications:  

1) TIN verification: We will run the W-9 TIN through our IRS verification process. If BlueHarbor can supply a 147C it will speed this step; otherwise our verification usually completes within 48 hours once submitted.

2) Escrow agreement execution: Samir — please confirm you can accept DocuSigned signature for the escrow agreement and confirm expected hold-window start date (we need alignment for invoicing).

Next steps and owner:  
- Marta: please upload the delegation letter and photo ID for Diego to the secure procurement folder (link below) by EOD Monday.
- Samir: return a DocuSign-ready escrow agreement redline within 24 hours if possible.
- Laura: I’ll queue the PO for conditional release after TIN verification completes.

If all items are received and KYC clears, we plan to release milestone 1 funds the week of 2025-04-21.

Thanks — I’ll update PO status in the procurement tracker.
